Source: Pew Research Center Analysis of Survey of Consumer Finances public-use data.

DATA:
- X-axis: Years (1983, 1992, 2001, 2007, 2010, 2013)
- Y-axis: Median household net worth ($) from 0 to 800K in increments of 100K
- Lower income:
  - 1983: ≈ 12K
  - 1992: ≈ 14K

- Middle income:

  - 1992: ≈ 96K
  - 2001: ≈ 137K
  - 2007: ≈ 161K
  - 2010: ≈ 99K
  - 2013: ≈ 100K
- Upper income:
  - 1983: ≈ 323K
  - 1992: ≈ 344K
  - 2001: ≈ 600K
  - 2007: ≈ 730K
  - 2010: ≈ 606K
  - 2013: ≈ 650K

KEY FACTS:
- Upper-income families consistently have a significantly higher median net worth than middle- and lower-income families across all years shown.
- Upper-income median net worth grew substantially from 323K in 1983 to a peak of 730K in 2007, before dropping slightly and ending at 650K in 2013.
- Middle-income median net worth remained relatively stagnant, hovering around 100K for most years, with a small peak at 161K in 2007.
- Lower-income median net worth stayed extremely low, remaining under 25K across all recorded years.
